$comment: Protein analysis, bench analysis and plotting.
`reading-frames` is the one task whose point is a TOOL CHOICE rather than a
value: the model must call the translator in all-frames mode with an ORF floor,
not just translate frame 1. Its assertion therefore pins the ORF line the
all-frames mode emits, which frame-1-only output does not contain.

tasks.instruction:
I have a peptide and I need its basic physico-chemical parameters before I order it: molecular weight, isoelectric point, and the extinction coefficient I should use for a A280 measurement.

MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQLEERLGLIEVQ

Plan a trypsin digest of this peptide for mass spectrometry, with no missed cleavages, and give me the monoisotopic [M+H]+ mass of every peptide.

MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQLEERLGLIEVQ

assertions.pattern: trypsin digest, 0 missed cleavage\(s\), monoisotopic \[M\+H\]\+ masses: 7 peptide\(s\)

assertions.note: one space, not the two the raw render uses: every regex is matched against whitespace-COLLAPSED text, so a pattern built from the un-collapsed output cannot match. The first version of this assertion carried the raw double space and failed offline.

tasks.instruction:
Is this 14-residue peptide amphipathic? Draw the helical wheel projection and give me the hydrophobic moment and the residue-class breakdown.

LKKLLKKLLKKLLK

assertions.pattern: helical wheel for residues 1-14 \(14 residues, 100°/residue, 3\.6 per turn\)
residue classes: hydrophobic 7, polar 0, acidic 0, basic 7

tasks.instruction:
Plot the Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy profile of this peptide with the standard window and tell me whether it contains a candidate transmembrane stretch. Report the GRAVY value too.

MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQLEERLGLIEVQ

assertions.pattern: no window average reaches the 1\.6 threshold

tasks.instruction:
Optimize this coding sequence for E. coli expression and tell me the GC content of the result and how long it is. Also remove any EcoRI site from it while you are at it, since I want to clone with EcoRI.

{seq:cds}

assertions.note: the optimized construct's own reported length and GC. The VALUES are not pinned: the task asks for the EcoRI-avoidance pass, and passing `avoid_enzymes` legitimately changes which synonymous codons are chosen, hence both numbers. The first version pinned the no-avoidance result (261 bp / 84.3%) and failed a correct `avoid_enzymes` answer — and 84.3% GC would in fact be a poor answer to give a user who wants to express the protein.

tasks.instruction:
I do not know which frame this ORF is in. Translate all six frames and report every open reading frame of at least 20 amino acids, with the frame it is in and its coordinates.

GGG{seq:cds}

assertions.note: a reverse-strand frame with no stop codon — the reason all six were requested

tasks.instruction: Here is a qPCR standard curve: dilution factors 1, 10, 100, 1000 with Ct values 15.0, 18.3, 21.6, 24.9. Fit the curve, give me the slope, the R² and the amplification efficiency, and tell me whether the efficiency is good enough to trust the assay.

assertions.pattern: standard curve from 4 points: Ct = 15 \+ -3\.3·log10\(relative quantity\)

tasks.instruction: I have fold-change data from two conditions: control = 1 with SD 0.1, knockdown = 6.65 with SD 0.9. Draw me a bar chart with error bars, and then draw a second scatter chart of x = 1,2,3,4 against y = 2.1,3.9,6.2,7.8 with a fitted line. Name the files fold.svg and fit.svg.

The qPCR run is in the workspace as ct.csv (columns sample, strain, ct). Compare the two strains as a box plot — I want to see the spread and any wells that failed, and I need the median Ct of each strain. Write it to ct-box.svg.

assertions.note: the per-series summary the tool renders
the failed well is reported as an outlier, not folded into the whisker

tasks.instruction: growth.csv in the workspace has time_h, strain and od600 columns for three strains. Plot the growth curves as one line chart with a line per strain, and tell me which strain grew least. Write it to growth.svg.

assertions.note: the group column must split the table into three series, not plot one jumbled line
the y extent of the real table, so the tool was given the data and not an empty frame

tasks.instruction: From the same ct.csv, show me the distribution of all twelve Ct values as a histogram so I can see how the run behaved overall. Write it to ct-hist.svg.

assertions.note: the bin count is chosen by the tool's own rule, so only its shape is pinned
the default binning rule is named in the output

tasks.instruction: For the same ct.csv, I want to see the SHAPE of the distribution per strain, not just a box — one of the strains has a failed well that a box hides. Draw it as a violin plot with the median and IQR marked, write it to ct-violin.svg, and tell me each strain's median and whether the outlier changes the shape.

de.csv in the workspace has a differential-expression table with gene, log2fc and p columns. Draw a volcano plot to de.svg and tell me which genes are both significantly changed AND substantially changed — I do not want genes that only move a little, or only look good on one of the two axes.

assertions.note: MYC (big fold, useless p) and PTEN (good p, no fold) must NOT be counted
the two genes the model must EXCLUDE — naming them as excluded is fine, so this only requires they were considered

tasks.instruction: expression.tsv is a wide table: the first column is the gene name and the rest are samples. Draw it as a heatmap to heatmap.svg, row-scaled so the genes are comparable, and tell me which genes separate the control columns from the kd columns.

assertions.note: the requested display transform is named in the output
negative values select the diverging ramp automatically
